doc_verification.detail: Live qdrant.tech and api.qdrant.tech both domain_blocked (network restriction) -> PARTIAL, not FAIL. Version verified via the qdrant v1.18.0 clone's vendored API reference docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json (exact version match). That spec documents StrictModeConfig.search_max_oversampling = 'Max oversampling value allowed in search.' and defines SearchParams with ONLY hnsw_ef/exact/quantization/indexed_only/acorn — there is NO top-level params.oversampling; the documented oversampling knob is params.quantization.oversampling ('Oversampling factor for quantization. Default is 1.0.', validate range min 1.0). The claim's probed knob (top-level params.oversampling) does not exist in the v1.18.x API reference, so the claim premise is unsupported by documentation: content_consistency FAIL. Endpoints points/query and points/search are real v1.18 endpoints: PASS.

execution_evidence.log_pattern: query oversampling=100.0: 200 (claim's main violation observation; sibling raw lines: 'query oversampling=1.5: 200', 'query oversampling=2.0: 200')

http_semantics.note: Observed as plain HTTP 200 success with a normal result body — not even a business error code; the cap is silently not applied. Source explains why: the sent top-level 'oversampling' key is dropped during serde deserialization (unknown field, no deny_unknown_fields), so the server never sees a value to reject. Values 0.5/1.0 (within cap) also 200 — acceptance is value-independent, consistent with key-ignored rather than cap-checked. Control hnsw_ef=64 (a real SearchParams field) correctly returned 400 on the same collection.

(vendored at docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json in the qdrant v1.18.0 clone, schema ~line 8087); SearchParams.quantization -> QuantizationSearchParams.oversampling: "Oversampling factor for quantization. Default is 1.0." with #[validate(range(min = 1.0))].

chain_trace.break_detail: First break at contract: no constraint exists for this claim (dispatch constraint_id empty; grep zero hits). Second break at doc semantics: the vendored v1.18.x OpenAPI contradicts the claim's premise — the probed knob does not exist in the documented API, so the 200s evidence an unknown-field-ignored artifact rather than a guardrail gap. Qdrant's own integration test in the same v1.18.0 tree (tests/openapi/test_strictmode.py:495-529, test_strict_mode_search_max_oversampling_validation) asserts the documented path params.quantization.oversampling above search_max_oversampling IS rejected with an 'oversampling' strict-mode error.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST /points/query -> CollectionQueryRequest::check_strict_mode (verification/mod.rs:160-175: verify() calls check_custom + check_search_params) -> CollectionQueryRequest::request_search_params() returns self.params: SearchParams (query.rs:182-184) -> SearchParams::check_custom (mod.rs:331-348) -> check_limit_opt(self.quantization.and_then(|i| i.oversampling), search_max_oversampling) and check_limit_opt(self.hnsw_ef, search_max_hnsw_ef). Prefetch recursion: CollectionQueryRequest::check_custom loops self.prefetch -> CollectionPrefetch::check_strict_mode (query.rs:141-145 and 187-233, its own request_search_params() = self.params). REST /points/search -> SearchRequestInternal::request_search_params() = self.params (search.rs:21-23) -> same SearchParams::check_custom. Because SearchParams (segment/types.rs:590-617) has no top-level oversampling field and no deny_unknown_fields, the script's top-level 'oversampling' JSON key is silently dropped at deserialization; the check reads quantization=None -> check_limit_opt(None, Some(1.0)) returns Ok (mod.rs:302 both-Some guard) -> 200. The control hnsw_ef=64 hit a real SearchParams field -> 400, exactly as logged.
